name: Psychedelic therapy for self-image
lead: Psychedelic therapy is the proposed use of drugs such as psilocybin, LSD and MDMA in mental health treatment, usually with preparation and integration sessions.[1] Its use for self-image is an experimental idea; research has focused on depression, PTSD, anxiety and substance use.[1]

The only item related to body image on the source page is a 2024 review in which a single psilocybin dose given for OCD symptoms raised insight in patients who also had body dysmorphic disorder, leading them to seek treatment.[1] Psychedelics remain Schedule I in the US and are generally limited to clinical trials.
infobox: Schedule I (US); trials or limited programs elsewhere

paras: A 2024 meta-analysis of psilocybin trials found antidepressant effects above placebo, and an FDA panel in 2024 voted against approving MDMA for PTSD.[1] Limitations include small samples, short follow-up and blinding problems.[1]
Contraindications include pregnancy, serious cardiovascular disease, SSRI or MAOI use, and a personal or family history of psychosis or bipolar I disorder.[1]
No studies found on self-image or looks-related distress. A 2024 review noted increased insight in OCD patients with body dysmorphic disorder after psilocybin.[1]

card.summary: Experimental idea of using psychedelics for body image; no direct studies, and the drugs are controlled substances.
card.note: Schedule I in the US; contraindicated with some medications and psychiatric histories.

quick.overview:
Psychedelic therapy uses drugs like psilocybin with guided sessions to treat mental health conditions. Using it for self-image is experimental.

No studies directly examine self-image outcomes.
quick.mechanism: Mechanisms are poorly understood; outcomes depend heavily on mindset and setting.
quick.risks: The drugs are Schedule I in the US. Contraindications include psychosis history, pregnancy and SSRI use.
